structure: This is one fixed, source-anchored scenario for the declared selected Turkana adult context, not an estimated Turkana population distribution. Recorded sex is Bernoulli. Conditional on sex, four standard Gaussian scores have the specified correlation matrix. Monotone transformations give age, BMI, TC and HDL. Uganda supplies adult age quantiles and sex-specific geometric-mean locations; Navrongo supplies relative-dispersion anchors; one rural Ashanti rank-correlation triple supplies BMI/lipid dependence through an explicit Gaussian-copula bridge. The source unadjusted rank triple is assumed transportable to within-recorded-sex ranks, not treated as adjusted Pearson evidence. Separate assumed latent age correlations complete the joint law. All pairwise latent correlations are nonzero. Sex-specific margins create additional pooled dependence. The requested analyses are raw-scale population linear projections of this nonlinear joint law. No finite-sample calibration, outcome-target matching or causal interpretation is used. Evidence paths below are relative to SOURCE_EVIDENCE_JSON; parameter paths refer to the returned object.

requested_estimands.derivation_or_reason_unavailable: Let X=(1,age,I(sex=F),bmi)^T, M=E[XX^T] and g_H=E[X*HDL], with HDL in mmol/L. The requested population value is 5*38.67 times the BMI component of M^{-1}g_H. This is equivalent to the supplied centered/scaled design. No numerical population projection has been evaluated here; age cross-moments require integration over the specified quantile transformation. Neither an input rank correlation nor a lognormal shape parameter is this estimand.

With X and M as above and g_T=E[X*TC] in mmol/L, the requested population value is 5*38.67 times the BMI component of M^{-1}g_T. No numerical population projection has been evaluated here. The complete joint law defines the value, but the supplied source statistics do not identify this age/sex-adjusted raw-scale target association.

Using the same X and M, define V_T=E[TC^2]-g_T^T M^{-1}g_T, V_H=E[HDL^2]-g_H^T M^{-1}g_H and C=E[TC*HDL]-g_T^T M^{-1}g_H. The population residual correlation is C/sqrt(V_T*V_H). Numerical unit conversion cancels. No numerical evaluation of these projection moments has been performed. This quantity is neither the rural unadjusted Spearman coefficient nor the Gaussian-copula latent correlation.

limitations: The target demographic and lifestyle composition is unidentified by the admitted evidence. Uganda-like age and geometric-mean locations, Navrongo-like relative dispersions and rural Ashanti-like rank dependence are explicit cross-population scenario assumptions, not a reconstruction of Turkana outcomes.

The construction does not reproduce every statistic from any external cohort. In particular, reference arithmetic moments supply only CVs, and source pooled rank relationships are reassigned to within-sex dependence by assumption.

Source health exclusions, age restrictions, laboratory methods and fasting protocols differ from the target. Applying no corresponding target filters does not eliminate selection or measurement-transfer bias.

The unadjusted or differently adjusted source regressions are deliberately unused. Agongo's unresolved log base and Greiner's unresolved regression transformations remain unresolved; smoking and alcohol adjustment sets are not silently reduced.
Age tails, lognormal measurement tails, Gaussian-copula dependence and common dependence across sex are unidentified modeling choices. No extra upper bounds or TC>=HDL exclusion are introduced.
All generated records are complete and analysis-eligible under the stated rules. This is a completeness assumption, not evidence about original target missingness or health status.

Finite generated samples will have sampling variation in all requested analyses. Such sample estimates must not be presented as exact population values or as uncertainty intervals covering transport and structural uncertainty.
Curator extraction records and their historical review claims are provenance only. No original article authentication, retrieval, execution or validation has been performed for this response.
